hpdi.title: H-P-D-I self-assessment
hpdi.subtitle: Leaders assess the organisation's digital maturity across four spaces: Human, Process, Data, Intelligence.
hpdi.forbidden: Only unit and department leaders can use this page.
hpdi.intro: Each question has 5 levels: pick the one that best describes what actually happens in the organisation today, not what you would like. A space's score is the average of its questions. Next to each space are figures Signet measures from the organisation's own data, for comparison.
hpdi.disclaimer: The questions were written by the Signet team, based on the H-P-D-I definitions in the OLP 2026 theme introduction and the DX-OS course book (sources at the bottom). This is a self-assessment tool, not an official government index, and it does not convert to a DTI score.
hpdi.managerNote: Department leaders can answer and see the result in this browser; only the unit leader saves results and sees the organisation's measured figures.
hpdi.fill: Fill in from the last saved run
hpdi.evidenceNone: Signet has no measured figures for this space in the organisation yet.
hpdi.evidenceHint: The organisation's figures when the page was opened, to compare with the answers; they are not used for scoring.

hpdi.focus: {space}: the lowest score in the part of the foundation that is not yet solid. Strengthen this space before investing in the later ones.
hpdi.focusLast: {space}: the lowest score; the three foundation spaces before it all score higher. This is where to invest next.
hpdi.focusNone: All four spaces are at level 5: keep the pace and reassess regularly.
hpdi.gapsNone: None: no later space is ahead of the one before it.
hpdi.gapsHint: Following the linear evolution principle H → P → D → I: a later space built on an earlier one that is not solid easily turns into “garbage in, garbage out”.

diamond.name: Complete diamond
diamond.text: [P], [D] and [I] all reach near the top and little work is manual: processes stop errors, data is clean, AI runs on a solid base.

illusion.name: Technology illusion
illusion.text: [D] or [I] is ahead of [P]: analytics or AI built before the process foundation, so careless data entry turns into wrong results.

kite.name: Off-centre kite
kite.text: [P] is solid but [D] and [I] are almost absent: work follows the process, but there are no figures to steer by (blind execution).

spear.name: Fragmented spear
spear.text: Most work still rests on people and [P], [D], [I] stay near the centre: the unit depends on a few key staff.

transitional.name: In transition
transitional.text: None of the four archetypes in the course book fits; see the foundation gaps and the space to work on first.

hpdi.shares: Shares estimated as in the course book: [H] {h} % · [P] {p} % · [D] {d} % · [I] {i} %
hpdi.shapeHint: From the DX-OS course book, section 2.4 (Dr Tạ Tuấn Anh, CC BY 4.0): [P], [D] and [I] each take at most 30 %, converted from the score (level 1 is 0 %, level 5 is 30 %); [H] is the work left on people, 100 % minus the other three, not the [H] space score. The book also multiplies by an evidence factor; here it is 1 because every level already describes observable practice. A guide only, not a DTI score.
hpdi.gigo: Intelligence and analytics rest on a weak base: [I] is above [D], or [D] and [I] are ahead of [P]. AI and reports that learn from wrong data give wrong results. Pause expanding [I] (agent suggestions, AI questions), standardise [P] and [D] first, and check the data quality flags of the reports:
hpdi.saveHint: Each save is one row in the organisation's history and one audit log entry; it cannot be edited or deleted. The system recomputes the scores from the answers.
hpdi.historyNone: The organisation has not saved any run yet.

sensors.title: Storage sensor map
sensors.subtitle: Latest temperature of each room in the records storage against the alert threshold, with sensor data quality flags. Refreshes every 30 seconds.
sensors.forbidden: This page is for clerks, staff, department heads and unit directors.

offHint.off: No NGSI-LD context broker is configured to receive sensor readings (MOC_NGSI_URL of svc-workflow). Contact your system administrator.
offHint.unavailable: The NGSI-LD context broker (iot profile) is not running or not answering yet, so there are no readings. Administrators enable it with make demo-it-ot or docker compose --profile iot up -d.

sensors.planLabel: Floor plan of the records storage, each room coloured by its latest temperature against the threshold
sensors.panHint: Scroll horizontally to see the full plan. Detailed readings are listed below.
sensors.outsideHint: {n} sensor(s) declare no room code (room attribute) or a code that is not on the plan: listed in the table only.
sensors.threshold: Alert threshold {threshold} (MOC_OT_THRESHOLD). Above it, the system drafts an "Incident report" for the staff member responsible for the sensor.

levelHint.near: above {from}, up to {threshold}; a hint only, no alert is sent
levelHint.unknown: no reading yet, signal lost or out of range

flagHint.stale: no new reading for more than {n} minutes
flagHint.out_of_range: value is not a number, or outside the sensor's measuring range ({min} to {max})
flagHint.duplicate_time: the latest reading has the same observation time (observedAt) as another reading: stuck device clock or replayed message
flagHint.future_time: the latest reading's observation time (observedAt) is more than {slack} minutes ahead of the server clock: device clock running fast; signal loss is then judged by when the broker received the reading

sensors.flagsNote: Flags are computed by the server from the sensor's digital twin in the context broker; rooms flagged signal lost or out of range are not coloured by the reading.
